text:
ops-bot: [ALERT] 2178901234 - SLO breach detected for /v1/stream (region: us-west-2). p95=1.1s, p99=3.6s (5m window) :rotating_light:
ryan (oncall): seeing this on alerts, paging SRE. is this a routing flap or origin saturation?
maya (sre): starting a quick investigation. can someone dump the top errors from the edge proxies?
alex (infra): pulling envoy metrics now, seeing increased upstream timeouts to streaming-backend pool (streamers-prod-usw2-*)
alex (infra): envoy upstream_5xx: spike coincident with p99. Also saw keepalive-writes failing to drain on some sockets.
ryan (oncall): reproducible with a simple curl stream test?
maya (sre): yes - here's a quick check i ran from a box in usc2: 
```
curl -N -v "https://api.redwood.ai/v1/stream?model=redwood-stream" -H "Authorization: Bearer xxxxx"
* Connected to api.redwood.ai (54.###.###.###) port 443 (#0)
> GET /v1/stream?model=redwood-stream HTTP/1.1
> Host: api.redwood.ai
> User-Agent: curl/7.68.0
> Accept: */*
>
* SSL connection using TLS1.3
< HTTP/1.1 200 OK
< content-type: text/event-stream
\n// first chunk arrives, then stalls for ~7s\n```
ryan (oncall): that stall matches the p99 window. looks like chunks are delayed not dropped.
cs-amy: we have reports from 6 paying customers about choppy streaming in the last 20m, one is doing payments flow. tagging product/security.
eng-runtime: likely candidate: a new KV-cache GC bump and a concurrent GC on some GPU-serving nodes causing occasional stall while kernel preemption occurs. also seen client-side write backpressure build-up in the proxy when large payloads come through.
maya (sre): ok next: isolate whether stalls are from origin (runtime) or proxy (envoy). running tcpdump + proxy logs on a affected host.
alex (infra): increasing streamers-prod-usw2 pool size by +20% (scale-up) and enabling overflow routing to secondary pool (streamers-prod-usw2-b). applying now.
ops-bot: deploy-bot: started scaling action for streamers-prod-usw2 (delta +6 nodes). Link: https://console.redwood.ai/clusters/streamers-prod-usw2
ryan (oncall): enabling proxy keepalive tweaks to reduce stalled sockets. will flip `envoy.socket_acceptor.keepalive_timeout` from 60s -> 15s for the affected frontends (hotfix).
maya (sre): while that deploys, i pushed a short-lived config to force smaller chunk flushes from runtime (flush_interval_ms=50) — should reduce burst buffering.
eng-runtime: i see the runtime change rolled out to ~40% of nodes. monitoring tail latency.
maya (sre): quick look at metrics: p95 back to 0.9s, p99 down to 1.4s after initial scale+flush. still some residual stalls on ~3 hosts.
alex (infra): those 3 hosts show kernel thread preemption logs around the same times (OOM-killer? no) — looks like a long GC in the runtime process. collecting stack traces.
ryan (oncall): for customer comms: cs-amy, please gather the list of customers seeing streaming anomalies and whether any requests timed out or errors returned (5xx) vs stalls. prioritize the payments customer.
cs-amy: pulling customer logs, 7 customers with >50% of their streaming sessions affected, 2 customers had errors escalate to 502 from the proxy. reaching out to both account owners now.
eng-runtime: adding a temporary circuit-breaker to the proxy-to-runtime route to fail fast on high queue-depth — this will reduce tail amplification for other tenants. rolling now.
ops-bot: incident-bot: incident created -> INC-2026-217890. Severity: sev2. On-call: ryan. Escalation: eng-runtime, infra, cs.
ryan (oncall): handoff note: if anything degrades again, route traffic to fallback region (us-east-1) for the most critical routes. currently routing is still us-west primary.
maya (sre): mitigation status: scale-up complete, keepalive change rolled, flush_interval lowered, circuit-breaker active. observed decrease in stalled connections.
eng-runtime: stack traces show runtime thread stuck in `kv_cache::compact()` for ~4-6s on affected nodes. we'll push a GC-rate limiter in 10m to avoid long pauses.
ryan (oncall): customer impact summary for pager: ~0.8% of total streaming requests in last 30m affected, concentrated on 7 heavy-streaming customers. visible symptoms: stalls (most), a smaller % (~0.02%) got 502 from proxy timeouts.
cs-amy: sent initial outreach to the 7 accounts with incident summary + mitigation steps. asked them to DM if they still see issues.
maya (sre): monitoring window 30m post-mitigation: p99 trending down to ~0.9s, p95 ~0.7s. will keep watch for 1h.
ryan (oncall): recording runbook items: 1) scale streamers pool, 2) reduce flush interval, 3) lower keepalive, 4) enable circuit-breaker, 5) /postmortem with runtime GC investigation.
eng-runtime: queued a follow-up changelist to add non-blocking compaction and GC pacing. will include perf regression tests.
ryan (oncall): final note before handing to maya for wakeful watch: if no regressions in 1h, we can close the on-call page and start PM/PM postmortem.
maya (sre): taking handoff at 10:40 UTC — will monitor dashboards, ETA for GC fix is EOD.
ops-bot: paging-bot: ryan (oncall) acknowledged. :white_check_mark:
ryan (oncall): thanks team. creating follow-up ticket: STREAM-4862 (postmortem + runtime fix).
cs-amy: will update customer comms once we have postmortem draft.
eng-runtime: leaving a note to include reproducer script and a perf harness to emulate client backpressure patterns.
ryan (oncall): closing noise alert; will update incident timeline later.
maya (sre): 20m update: metrics continue to look stable, no new escalations. I'll keep monitoring and will kick off postmortem doc after EOD.
ops-bot: incident-bot: INC-2026-217890 status -> mitigation_in_progress
maya (sre): handing over to eng-runtime for root cause + fix work. oncall handoff complete.
eng-runtime: acknowledged, taking ownership of RCA and timeline.
